title: Connect a new bag-in-box syrup carton: twist the line's connector off the empty box's spout and lock it onto the new one
context: Changing an empty bag-in-box syrup carton for a full one is routine back-room work for fast food and counter workers (about 3.5 million in the US). The line's quick-disconnect connector is twisted a quarter turn and pulled off the empty box's spout; the new box's spout, pulled out through its knock-out, rides on the slack bag, so one hand holds it by its flange while the other pushes the connector on and turns its collar a quarter turn to lock it.
setup: Bench top is z = 0.7475 m (the bench is only the working height). A low chrome wire shelf (340 x 700 mm wire deck 120 mm up on four 25 mm grooved posts, levelling feet) stands centred at x 0.47, y 0. On its deck stand two 5-gallon (18.9 L) bag-in-box cola syrup cartons of white clay-coated corrugated board, printed with a fictional brand (red Velmora wordmark panel with a ribbon; Cola Syrup Concentrate, Bag-in-Box 5 gal (18.9 L), 5+1 mix ratio, nutrition panel, barcode, lot/best-by stamp, recycle and THIS SIDE UP marks), 273 x 273 x 394 mm (10.75 x 10.75 x 15.5 in), their knock-out faces toward the arms (face at x 0.334): the new carton (full, about 24 kg, fixed) centred at y -0.165, the empty carton at y 0.165. Each has a round 82 mm knock-out (dashed perforation, flap pushed in) whose centre is 65 mm above the carton's base. The new carton's bag spout, a white polyethylene BIB fitting (46 mm flange, 25 mm spout with an O-ring land, 40 mm long), has been pulled out through its knock-out: its flange stands 45 mm in front of the face (pulled out on the bag's neck), its spout pointing at the arms (axis at z 0.9325, y -0.165); it gives way into the carton when pushed. The empty carton's spout carries the syrup line's quick-disconnect connector: a white acetal body 32 mm across and 60 mm long with a red 40 mm ribbed locking collar with two thumb wings, 70 g, its 90-degree 3/8 in elbow barb clamped into translucent 9.5 mm syrup tubing, 1.14 m of it, which runs from the connector down to the bench in a loose loop and up to the pump's inlet. Along the bench's left edge a plywood pump board (440 x 18 x 450 mm) stands at y 0.445, face toward -y, with a black gas-driven BIB syrup pump (95 x 80 x 150 mm) on a steel bracket, its GAS / IN / OUT ports tagged and clamped, a blue CO2 line, and a bundle of three more syrup lines with coloured ID bands tied along the board's top.
scoring: 0.25: the connector is off the empty carton's spout (freed by a quarter turn counter-clockwise) and at least 30 mm from where it sat. 0.5: it is pushed onto the new spout square (within 3 mm of the spout's axis, 4 mm of fully on, 8 degrees). 0.75: it is turned a quarter turn clockwise on the new spout (85 degrees or more): locked. 1.0: also every pad point of both hands at least 5 cm from the connector's surface and the connector at rest (under 0.01 m/s and 0.5 rad/s), held 1 s. The 0.25 milestone latches once reached. The line pulled taut (its ends more than 95% of its 1.14 m length apart) or the new spout pushed more than 20 mm back into its carton (not held) cap the score at 0.5; the connector dropped below the shelf's deck caps it at 0.25.
reset_notes: Fixed poses, no randomisation: connector on the empty carton's spout (collar unturned), new spout pulled out to 45 mm in front of its carton's face, line drawn from the pump to the connector.
fidelity: PhysX 240 Hz. Cartons, rack and board fixed. The syrup line is 24 colliding capsule links (1.14 m) on D6 bend joints, fixed at the pump, jointed to the connector's elbow barb. The bag is not modelled: the new spout rides on a sprung slide (120 N/m), giving way unless held. The quarter-turn lock is a rule: damped hinges about the spout axis, freed or locked at 85 deg, joined when pushed on square. Print is an image texture of a made-up brand.
